description: A composite 4x4 panel of EBSD maps from a Fe-30Mn-10Al-1.5C-xBe low-density steel rolled at 1050 C. Rows are the four Be levels: (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be, (d) 1.5Be. Columns are four map types: (1) grayscale IQ (image quality) maps overlaid with grain-boundary lines; (2) multi-coloured IPF (inverse pole figure) orientation maps; (3) KAM (kernel average misorientation) maps; (4) phase maps. Scale bars read 100 um for rows (a)-(b) and 60 um for rows (c)-(d). A right-hand legend gives the RD (rolling direction) arrow (pointing up), the austenite IPF colour triangle with 001, 101, 111 corners, a KAM colour bar labelled "Color Coded Map Type: Kernel Average Misorientation" (Min 0, Max 4.99993, top block) and the phase key green = Austenite, red = Ferrite. In the phase maps (a4) and (b4) are entirely green austenite, (c4) adds scattered red ferrite patches, and (d4) shows large connected red ferrite regions, so ferrite fraction rises with Be. KAM maps are deep blue with green/yellow hot-spots decorating boundaries. The figure demonstrates that Be addition progressively converts the single-austenite matrix into an austenite-ferrite duplex structure.

subfigures.description: IQ (image quality) map of 0Be steel, grayscale, 100 um scale bar; dense equiaxed grain structure with dark grain-boundary network drawn in red/green/blue lines and scattered dark precipitates.
IPF orientation map of 0Be, 100 um scale bar; many multi-coloured equiaxed grains with fine, closely spaced boundaries.
KAM map of 0Be, 100 um scale bar; predominantly deep blue with sparse green/yellow hot-spots.
Phase map of 0Be, 100 um scale bar; almost entirely green (austenite) with no resolvable red ferrite.
IQ map of 0.5Be, 100 um scale bar; coarser grains than (a1), lighter contrast, boundary lines still present.
IPF orientation map of 0.5Be, 100 um scale bar; multi-coloured grains, several very large grains.
KAM map of 0.5Be, 100 um scale bar; blue matrix with slightly more green/yellow speckle than (a3).
Phase map of 0.5Be, 100 um scale bar; essentially all green (austenite) with only negligible red.
IQ map of 1.0Be, 60 um scale bar; darker, precipitate-decorated boundaries, smaller field of view.
IPF orientation map of 1.0Be, 60 um scale bar; multi-coloured grains with mixed low- and high-angle boundaries.
KAM map of 1.0Be, 60 um scale bar; broader and more uniform green/yellow distribution across grains.
Phase map of 1.0Be, 60 um scale bar; green austenite with scattered red ferrite patches along boundaries and in bands.
IQ map of 1.5Be, 60 um scale bar; dense dark precipitates decorating grain boundaries.
IPF orientation map of 1.5Be, 60 um scale bar; grains with many blue low-angle (1-5 deg) boundary lines inside them.
KAM map of 1.5Be, 60 um scale bar; densest and most uniform green/yellow misorientation speckle of the series.
Phase map of 1.5Be, 60 um scale bar; green austenite matrix with large connected red ferrite regions, the most ferrite of any panel.

observations.observation: The group is a 4x4 array of EBSD-derived maps; rows are Be levels 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be, columns are IQ, IPF, KAM and phase maps.
Scale bars read 100 um on the (a) and (b) rows and 60 um on the (c) and (d) rows, so the two blocks have different magnifications.
The phase maps use green for Austenite and red for Ferrite, as given by the legend at the lower right.
Phase map (a4) for 0Be is entirely green with no resolvable red, whereas (d4) for 1.5Be contains large red ferrite regions; (c4) for 1.0Be shows only scattered red patches.
A RD (rolling direction) arrow is drawn in the upper-right legend area of the figure.
The KAM colour bar is labelled Min 0 and Max 4.99993 in the upper block and Max 4.93816 in the lower block, with Fraction values printed alongside.
The IPF legend triangle in the upper block is labelled Austenite with 0 0 1, 1 0 1 and 1 1 1 corners; the lower block shows separate Austenite and Ferrite triangles.
The caption states that (a), (b), (c) and (d) show the 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be cases for the IQ map, the IPF map, the KAM map and the Phase map respectively.
The citing text states that blue lines mark large-angle grain boundaries (>15 deg), green lines small-angle boundaries (5-15 deg) and red lines boundaries of 1-5 deg.
The citing text states that the KAM maps show stress concentration at the precipitation sites of carbide and Be-Fe phase, concentrated at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
The citing text states that the ferrite content in the matrix gradually increases with increasing Be content, with red indicating ferrite and green austenite.
The citing text states that the stress concentration in Fig. 13(c3, d3) shows a relatively uniform distribution.
The figure is of the Fe-30Mn-10Al-1.5C-xBe (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) steel rolled at 1050 C, as stated in the caption and citing text.
